ruling.recommended_action: Record the RD-1 route-deviation breach on the driver's file (no fare refund: RydeX is a fixed-fare service and the billed distance equals the optimal route); no account flag is warranted because the upheld segment is not a non-exempt segment.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeX is a non-metered, fixed-quote service: the fare is quoted at booking and in-trip mileage does not change it [F6], so the traced RD-2 branch (detour km entering the fare) fails and no refund formula applies [RD-2]. The billed distance of 10.68 km does not exceed the optimal 10.7 km [F4][F6], so no excess mileage was charged; the complaint itself concedes the fare was a fixed quote.

One off-route segment is measured: 14:19–14:26, 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km and reaching up to 1160 m from the optimal route [F3]. That is a deviation from the driver's shortest-and-most-direct obligation [RD-1].

The driver's excuse fails: no traffic incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F11], and the two speed-band records at band 4 (30–39 km/h) are neither band 1 nor 2 and cover expressways not tied to the replaced optimal stretch, so they cannot exempt the segment on their own [F9][F10][RD-4]. His "the GPS rerouted me" statement is a post-trip claim, not consent, and in any case is not a reasonable cause [F8][RD-4][RD-5].

Consent cannot be found. There are no in-app messages at all between rider and driver [F7], so no rider message was sent before the segment began at 14:19; the only agreement-like assertion is in the driver's own post-trip statement, which does not constitute consent [F8][RD-5]. No stop was requested or measured in the segment, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt it either [F3][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts as a non-exempt deviation [RD-1][RD-2][RD-5].

Because the service is fixed-fare, the non-exempt segment yields a refundable amount of zero and the outcome is no_action, with the RD-1 breach recorded [RD-2]. The RD-6 flag is not applied: the flag prerequires a refund greater than zero or a recorded RD-1 violation treated as a basis for account review, and this ruling records the breach without an account action; the driver's two prior upheld route disputes over 90 days [F14] support flagging only when a non-exempt segment is found, which is not the case here [RD-6][F14].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and the (empty) chat; I found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — "The GPS rerouted me, that's all" is a route remark, not abuse [F8][F7][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment, both traffic records, the absence of incidents and the absence of chat are all in the record [F3][F7][F9][F10][F11]; the fare is fixed so no rate arithmetic is needed [F6][RD-2].

Driver advocate brief is empty and requests no_action; the underlying driver position ('GPS rerouted me, nothing wrong with the fare') is rejected as a reasonable-cause excuse — no traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F11], speed bands alone do not exempt [F9][F10] [RD-4] — and as consent, since a statement made after the trip is not rider consent [F8][F7][RD-5].

The segment is therefore non-exempt under RD-1/RD-2.

Because your fare was a fixed quote agreed at booking, the extra distance did not change what you were charged, so there is nothing to refund. We have recorded the route deviation on the driver's file, and his account is now going to account review given similar upheld complaints before. No further action is needed from you.

No traffic incident was recorded on that stretch, the speed records you cited do not cover it, and there was no message from the rider agreeing to the detour, so the segment counts as a breach of your shortest-and-most-direct route duty and is recorded on your file. No refund is due, since the fare was a fixed quote and the billed distance did not exceed the optimal route. Your account is going to account review because of this and earlier upheld route complaints.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:19:10 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts.
